severity_cases.given: A domain module executes infrastructure work while it is imported.
severity_cases.rationale: Import-time side effects make every consumer pay infrastructure cost and can fail before application startup is controlled.

severity_cases.given: A domain model has a static dependency on infrastructure.
severity_cases.rationale: The dependency violates model purity and increases change coupling, but a static edge alone is not an import-time execution failure.

severity_cases.given: A use case or application service imports a concrete adapter instead of a domain port.
severity_cases.rationale: The application layer is coupled to infrastructure selection; dependency injection through a port restores the intended boundary.

severity_cases.given: A dependency edge points in a forbidden direction and does not match a more specific severity case.
severity_cases.rationale: Unmatched structural inversions break the slice dependency contract and require immediate correction.

growth_cases.given: An event dispatcher is introduced to break a cross-slice cycle.
growth_cases.rationale: The dispatcher removes a concrete cycle and is a canonical exception to the pressure-first growth signal.

growth_cases.given: A one-file positional crust marks internal visibility in a language without another privacy mechanism.
growth_cases.rationale: The directory is a visibility boundary rather than speculative growth structure, even when it contains one file.

growth_cases.given: A new abstraction has one concrete consumer and no demonstrated pressure.
growth_cases.rationale: The normal two-concrete-consumer signal has not been met, so the abstraction should be challenged as premature rather than treated as a blocker.
